A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VideoNIAH and VNBench. Their complete main texts, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support matching retained, relocated and newly added content.

before.justification: V1 reports original VNBench evaluations, model-setting experiments, task correlations, circular-evaluation robustness tests and VNBench-Long results.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark results and adds evaluations of newer models and experiments involving model size, frame sampling, token density and temporal prompts.

M1.justification: The proposed VideoNIAH construction procedure and instantiated VNBench tasks remain unchanged. CLIP filtering moves from v1 Appendix D.3 to v2 Section 3.3; it is not a new component. The additional model configurations serve the experimental analyses.

E1.justification: V2 adds original model-training experiments using Cauldron image-text instructions and ten video-text datasets, including ShareGPT4Video, TextVR and CLEVRER (Appendix F). This substantially expands the data actually used by the work. VNBench and VNBench-Long evaluation coverage remains unchanged.

E2.justification: V2 adds Qwen2-VL-7B and LLaVA-OneVision at 0.5B, 7B and 72B to the main and duration-specific comparisons (Tables 2 and 6). These additions substantially strengthen the evaluated open-model comparison set while retaining the original model families.

E3.justification: Section 6 introduces training-based protocols varying frame tokens from 25 to 196, sampled frames from 8 to 128, and temporal prompts, with stated controls. Benchmark scoring remains unchanged. V2 also labels the inherited 10.8 LLaMA-VID result as 7B, although v1 Table 4 associates it with 13B; an actual configuration change or rerun is not established.

E4.justification: V1's compact VideoChat2 sampling and LLaMA-VID size study is replaced by broader model-size, frame-count, token-density and temporal-prompt analyses in v2 Section 6. Token allocation and explicit temporal cues introduce new investigative questions. Existing needle-position, task-correlation and circular-evaluation robustness analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The one-to-four-iteration circular-evaluation analysis and its reporting remain unchanged (v1 Appendix H; v2 Appendix E). Neither version provides training-seed repetitions, confidence intervals or error bars, and v2 introduces no new uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: Shared main-table numerical entries are retained. Newly evaluated OneVision-72B scores 58.7 overall, making it the strongest reported open model versus ST-LLM's 22.7 in v1; Gemini remains at 66.7. V2 also adds substantial configuration-study results, including overall scores of 29.3–36.5 across temporal prompts, while removing v1 Table 4's specific ablation entries.

T1.justification: The work remains an empirical benchmark study with procedural task descriptions. V2 adds no substantive mathematical definitions, formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: V2 makes minimally confounded, skill-specific diagnosis during iterative model development a central claim. It recasts the tasks around temporal perception, chronological ordering and spatio-temporal coherence, and adds model-training guidance to the stated contributions. V1 primarily emphasized comprehensive fine-grained, spatio-temporal and long-context evaluation.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds interpretations linking model scale, frame sampling and temporal prompts to particular capabilities, and uses token-density results to argue for primarily temporal assessment. Section 7 replaces v1's mainly future-expansion limitations with an explicit qualification that synthetic evaluation cannot fully reproduce authentic scenarios and should complement real-world benchmarks.

D1.justification: V2 Appendix F documents the trained SigLIP/Qwen2 model, training mixture, context length, batch size, component-specific learning rates and schedule. Appendix C.1 adds sampling and resolution details for new baselines. Conversely, v1's explicit dataset-license disclosure and VNBench-Long sample-count column disappear; the code/data link remains.

R1.justification: V2 adds recent benchmark references, including VideoMME, MLVU, MMWorld and LongVideoBench, alongside new model and backbone references. More substantively, it develops a critique of comprehensive benchmarks for entangling multiple skills, expanding the positioning beyond v1's emphasis on construction cost and data leakage.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and task explanations are substantially rewritten. Detailed task construction moves into Appendix A.4, filtering moves into the main text, and dedicated model-analysis and revised limitations sections reshape the narrative. The appendices are reorganized, with the societal-impact and accessibility sections removed.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially redrawn and a new construction overview becomes Figure 2; the original task diagram survives as Figure 13. V2 adds three model-analysis plots and new prompt/training tables, expands result tables, removes v1's benchmark-comparison table, and changes typography and page layout throughout.

improvement.justification: V2 provides more useful evidence for model diagnosis through its controlled token, frame and prompt studies, and better qualifies synthetic evaluation's applicability. These support a limited net improvement over v1's smaller setting study. Gains are tempered by new reporting inconsistencies: OneVision-72B Counting-E2 is 14.7 in Table 2 but 36.0, 38.0 and 18.0 across Table 6's duration splits. The explicit dataset-license disclosure is also lost.
